articleTitle: Electrical impedance tomography/applied potential tomography-physiological imaging of the lungs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrical Impedance Tomography/Applied Potential Tomography
abstract: The author discusses clinical applications of electrical impedance tomography using the Sheffield applied potential tomography system. The examples given are: diagnosis of ventilation deflects; monitoring intrathoracic fluid volumes; continuous monitoring of ventilation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Single step algorithms for image reconstruction. II. Generalisation of the Sheffield filtered back projection algorithm. (Electric impedance tomography)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrical Impedance Tomography/Applied Potential Tomography
abstract: For pt.I see ibid. paper 4 (1992). The Sheffield system reconstructs images by a filtered back projection algorithm. To date the images have been produced from data originating from the adjacent drive configuration. However in principle the algorithm can be extended to reconstruct data originating from any bipolar drive configuration. Details of the various components of the image reconstruction process are given. Particular attention is paid to those areas where modifications are required to allow the technique to be extended to any dipolar drive configuration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrical Impedance Tomography/Applied Potential Tomography
abstract: The author compared three different multifrequency electric impedance tomography systems on a common basis using the Cardiff Phantom. The objective comparison of the data acquisition systems for tissue characterisation is reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrical Impedance Tomography/Applied Potential Tomography
abstract: The author discusses the use of electrical impedance tomographic imaging for providing information or thermal changes induced in tissue during hyperthermia treatment. Both superficial and deep body hyperthermia treatment are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrical Impedance Tomography/Applied Potential Tomography
abstract: The authors describe the development of the Oxford multiple drive system, OXPACT-II, which features current field generation applied through programmable voltage sources. The system, under microcomputer control, operates at 9.6 kHz and comprises 32 driving and 32 voltage measurement electrodes. The system performance of OXPACT-II has been evaluated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prospects for pulmonary and ventricular blood volume measurements using EIT
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrical Impedance Tomography/Applied Potential Tomography
abstract: Existing EIT systems provide a non-invasive method for assessing the fractional change in resistivity in fairly well defined regions of interest within the perimeter of the measurement electrodes. It should therefore be possible to obtain estimates of parameters of clinical importance such as cardiac output, and to be sure that they are kept separate from associated effects of, for example, pulmonary perfusion. The performance of one existing system is described and some prospects are surveyed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
